trust_decision.summary: Bytes of an untrusted tar header's octal numeric field (size, mode, checksum, and uid/gid/mtime when not base-256) are trusted to be octal digits; readOctal accepts any byte, so a byte below '0' gives a negative size that leaves the unpacker stuck in body state and buffering input without bound.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'malformed octal size field'. readOctal is the only octal decoder, and it is reached from parseUstarHeader's size read at src/tar/header.ts:141 via readNumeric.

fix_sites.entry_point: unpackTar (web, buffered) src/web/helpers.ts:141; createTarDecoder src/web/unpack.ts:39; unpackTar (fs) src/fs/unpack.ts:42; all go through createUnpacker src/tar/unpacker.ts:20 -> parseUstarHeader src/tar/header.ts:128
fix_sites.module_kind: shared low-level parsing primitive (internal module src/tar)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The fix sits in the one shared primitive, so every decoder is covered by one line. There is no second octal parser in src (only src/tar/encoding.ts:80 does the '- 48' digit decode).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No uncovered site to dismiss. At most, a solver might patch only the size field, or only the streaming decoder, because the buffered unpackTar already guards size < 0 (src/web/helpers.ts:238). A central fix in readOctal makes that moot.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Spaces and NUL inside octal fields must still parse (common space- or NUL-terminated and space-padded fields). Base-256 numeric fields (high bit set) must still decode. Non-strict mode must skip an invalid header block and continue to the next valid entry instead of aborting.

O6_input_shapes: byte below '0' (e.g. '/') giving a negative digit
bytes '8' and '9', which are not octal
on both file and pax-header typeflags (meta-header path src/tar/unpacker.ts:136-155)

O7_producer.where: Size is produced directly by parseUstarHeader src/tar/header.ts:141. PAX size override is validated separately by regex at src/tar/header.ts:171-174.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: PAX uid/gid use parseInt(v,10) without the strict digit regex that PAX size has; a planted PAX size parser using parseInt/Number would allow a negative or partial size override applied at src/tar/unpacker.ts:177-178.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The size mapper at src/tar/header.ts:171-174 is a hardened outlier next to looser sibling mappers; a maintainer could easily have written size with parseInt like uid/gid.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The base-256 branch masks the sign bit (0x7f) rather than handling 0xff negative encodings; a variant that honours the sign would produce a negative size via a route that never calls readOctal.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: GNU base-256 is signed, and a maintainer adding 'full POSIX support' could add two's-complement decoding.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The unpacker itself never rejects archiveSize < 0 (only the buffered helper does, at src/web/helpers.ts:238), so a defence placed only in one consumer is a realistic partial guard.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The defence already exists in one of the three consumers, which shows the project's pattern of consumer-local guards.

O9_family: CWE-1284 improper validation of specified quantity in input (non-octal digit in tar numeric field -> negative size -> unbounded buffering)

O10_build.project_tests: vitest --project node (package.json:53); tests/web/decoder.test.ts covers the decoder; the fix adds tests/tar/numeric.test.ts

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a size < 0 / NaN guard in the streaming decoder or unpacker for the size field only, leaving '8'/'9' digits and other readOctal consumers (mode, checksum) accepting garbage.

out_of_scope_notes: Meta-header size limit (MAX_META_SIZE) at src/tar/unpacker.ts:137 is a separate resource bound, not examined further.
